name: fanotify_mark
synopsis: int fanotify_mark(int fanotify_fd, unsigned int flags, uint64_t mask, int dirfd, const char *_Nullable pathname);
description: fanotify_mark() adds, removes, or modifies an fanotify mark on a filesystem object for event notifications. The caller must have read permission on the object and provide a file descriptor from fanotify_init(2).

parameters.name: fanotify_fd
parameters.description: File descriptor returned by fanotify_init(2) for the fanotify group

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Bitmask specifying the operation (e.g., FAN_MARK_ADD, FAN_MARK_REMOVE) and options (e.g., FAN_MARK_DONT_FOLLOW)

parameters.name: mask
parameters.description: Bitmask of events to listen for, ignore, or modify

parameters.name: dirfd
parameters.description: Directory file descriptor or AT_FDCWD for relative paths

parameters.name: pathname
parameters.description: Pathname of the filesystem object to mark

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set

errors.description: An invalid file descriptor was passed in fanotify_fd or dirfd is invalid
The mark cannot be updated due to conflicts, such as attempting to make an evictable mark on a non-evictable one
Invalid flags or mask, or incompatible arguments (e.g., invalid combination with FAN_MARK_MOUNT)
Operation requires a directory but the specified path is not one
The filesystem object is not associated with a filesystem that supports fsid
The filesystem object specified by dirfd and pathname does not exist
Insufficient memory to allocate necessary resources
Exceeded the limit on the number of marks for the user
The kernel does not support fanotify_mark()
The path is not a directory when required by flags or mask
The filesystem does not support file handle encoding
The caller lacks the required capability (e.g., CAP_SYS_ADMIN)
The filesystem object is in a subvolume with a different fsid
